en.headline: Japanese lifestyle retailer LOFT returns to Hong Kong with one-year pop-up at MOKO
en.dek: After a 15-year absence the stationery and novelty specialist opened on Saturday at Mong Kok’s New Century Plaza, stocking about 3,500 products of which half are exclusive to the local market.
body: Japanese lifestyle and stationery retailer LOFT reopened in Hong Kong on 22 August after a 15-year absence, launching a one-year limited store at MOKO in Mong Kok under YAICHI Group, the same operator that brought 3COINS to the city.

The shop at Level 1, Shop 141, 193 Prince Edward Road West offers roughly 3,500 items across five zones—health and beauty, creative homeware, selected Japanese foods, stationery and paper goods, and seasonal gifts—with about half the range exclusive to Hong Kong. Doors opened at 11 a.m.; more than 30 people were already queuing half an hour earlier and staff managed entry in batches as crowds filled the floor.

A LOFT representative said opening-day attendance met expectations and expressed hope the pop-up would lead to wider expansion. YAICHI founder Elmas Lou noted eight-figure investment and said the group would consider extending or adding outlets if performance is strong. Membership pricing under the YAICHI LOFT TOMO scheme references Japanese retail prices adjusted for the yen-HK dollar rate.

zh.headline: 日本生活雜貨店LOFT闊別15年重返香港 旺角MOKO設一年限定店
zh.dek: 文具及創意雜貨品牌周六於旺角新世紀廣場開業，店內約3,500款產品中有半數為香港限定，由引入3COINS的YAICHI集團營運。
body: 日本生活及文具雜貨專門店LOFT闊別香港15年後，於8月22日以一年期間限定店形式重返，進駐旺角MOKO新世紀廣場，由早前引入3COINS的YAICHI（谷日百貨）集團營運。
店舖位於太子道西193號MOKO 1樓141號舖，提供約3,500款產品，涵蓋健康美妝、創意家居、日本精選食品、文具紙品及時令禮品五大區域，當中約一半為香港限定。店舖上午11時開門，開門前半小時已有逾30人排隊，其後職員需分批安排顧客進場。
LOFT代表表示首日人流符合預期，並希望此次期間限定店成為進一步擴展的起點。YAICHI創始人羅盛昌指投資達八位數，若業績理想會考慮延長租約或增設分店。會員計劃YAICHI LOFT TOMO參考日本零售價及日圓匯率定價。
